meta_description: Search relevance rebuilt with retrieval evaluation — conversion from search up 7% and zero-result sessions down 68%

blocks.x: Search relevance rebuilt with retrieval evaluation, conversion from search up 7% and zero-result sessions down 68%

A specialty marketplace: Retail chains feel decision gaps in margin per store, visible in the weekly numbers. The Achala program started with the pricing and availability flow —. The baseline signed in week two made the cost visible in units the finance team already owns, and the engagement ran under the standard Achala charter — a named metric, a named control owner and gates that evidence every move.

The baseline fortnight measured the gap: 31% of search sessions ending without a click, zero-result pages on 9% of queries, and merchandising hand-tuning synonyms in a spreadsheet nobody fully trusted.

The catalog's metadata was seller-written and uneven; relevance was keyword-shaped while intent was need-shaped. No evaluation existed for any change, relevance shipped on opinion and rolled back on complaint.

We rebuilt search as an evaluated retrieval system: intent models over query and browse signals, hybrid retrieval spanning text and catalog attributes with seller-quality weighting, and, the actual unlock, an evaluation harness of labeled query sessions that every change must beat before shipping. Zero-result pages now trigger grounded query rewriting instead of a shrug.
